[SCENE GEOMETRY & ARCHITECTURE]
A medium format 6x7 architectural documentary photograph captured with a sharp wide-angle 45mm lens at f/8 on fine-grain film, presenting an elevated three-quarter bird's-eye perspective of the intersection at Charlotte Lane in Edinburgh. The urban fabric comprises plumb, rectilinear multi-storey Georgian terraces of dressed Craigleith blonde sandstone ashlar alongside a distinct 3-storey late-Victorian Tudor-revivalist corner building featuring decorative dark timber framing, off-white rendered infill panels, and a steeply pitched terracotta-tiled multi-gabled roof with tall brick chimneys. Symmetrical timber sash-and-case fenestration aligns across perfectly horizontal floor bands. Roofscapes display natural blue-grey Scottish slates, lead valleys with subtle white oxidation, and zinc flashing. The street surfaces consist of authentic, uneven whinstone cobblestone setts and broad sandstone kerbs, free of all motor traffic, pedestrians, and clutter, complemented by the organic foliage of a mature broadleaf leafy tree within an adjacent courtyard.
